summary.headline: Shaily Q1 FY27 revenue rose 14% YoY to INR281 crore, with Healthcare up 85% to INR142 crore, now the largest segment at 51%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 14% YoY to INR281 crore and EBITDA rose 18% to INR83 crore, with EBITDA margin up 120 bps to 29.7%. PAT rose 17% to INR48 crore (PAT margin 17.1%). Healthcare drove growth while Consumer fell 24% on softer European and US home furnishing demand. Management flagged sequential gross margin pressure from polymer and freight costs, with pass-throughs lagging into July, and said it expects normalisation by Q3.

segments.name: Healthcare
segments.commentary: Revenue INR142 crore, +85% YoY, driven by pen injectors for GLP-1 and other chronic therapies. Orders received after Semaglutide approvals in Canada and Brazil; two new platform projects signed.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.commentary: Revenue INR116 crore, -24% YoY on softer home furnishing demand in Europe and US. Management said Q4 to Q1 sequential revenue grew, and the business is expected to stay near FY26 levels in FY27.

segments.name: Industrial
segments.commentary: Revenue INR23 crore, +25% YoY, supported by new customers and Consumer Electronics and Appliance/Automotive business confirmations; five Consumer Electronics components won from a new customer.

guidance_outlook: FY27 pen injector guidance of 36 million pens; management said it should be able to go beyond 36 million, though it is evolving.
Additional 25 million pen capacity expected operational by end-September 2026, taking installed capacity to ~75 million pens per annum.
Gross margin expected to return to normalised levels by Q3 FY27 as delayed pass-throughs take effect.
Semiconductor revenue expected to start in Q4 FY27.
Abu Dhabi plant must be in production by end-FY28; commercial sales from end-FY28. About 50-55% commitments/indications secured for that capacity.
Management said 24-30 months to reach ~$10 million revenue in Consumer Electronics; stated as projection, not guidance.
Management declined to give UK subsidiary growth guidance; said Q1 UK revenue dip is timing and will recover over the next 3 quarters.
capex_capacity: New pen line: speed raised ~9% so far; additional equipment not yet received, expected to add ~30% throughput; target before end of Q1 FY27 (quarter end). Second line to ship only after supplier reaches 80%+ efficiency and passes FAT.
Additional 25 million pen capacity operational by end-September 2026.
Semiconductor Trays: about INR5 crore investment in existing facility for initial requirements.
Consumer Electronics: planned new plant in south India with investment of INR80-100 crore; land secured (not yet announced). Start-up update expected next quarter.
Consumer Electronics components to be supplied from existing facility, with tooling and automation investment required.
Abu Dhabi plant: sales by end-FY28, aimed at European opening in 2028 and insulin and global markets in 2030-31.
demand_pricing: Healthcare: Management estimates device volumes of ~9 million pens in Q1 (all delivery devices); mix roughly 50-60% GLP-1, remainder insulin and other molecules.
Pricing is volume and market-driven with annual price review, not cost-plus; index references include inflation and polymers, with contract longevity a key factor.
Chinese GLP-1 pens reportedly priced at $1.50-1.70 vs Shaily's above $2; management said some Chinese products infringe patents and it is considering a response.
Gross margin fell sequentially due to post-March commodity and freight cost spikes, premium airfreight, and delayed pass-throughs.
Consumer: softer home furnishing demand in Europe and US; India is ~2% of Consumer sales.
Management said it expects the Canada and Brazil positions to remain majority or significant share; expects Mexico, Turkey and Saudi Arabia to open up.

qa_highlights.question: How many pens were delivered in Q1 and what is the GLP-1 vs insulin mix?
qa_highlights.answer: About 9 million devices in Q1; roughly 50-60% GLP-1 with the rest insulin and other molecules.

qa_highlights.question: Is the new line on track and is FY27 36 million pens guidance beatable?
qa_highlights.answer: Line speed up about 9%, with extra equipment expected to add ~30%; 80%+ efficiency targeted before shipping the second line. Management said it should be able to go beyond 36 million.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline and pricing versus Chinese competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Margin dip due to commodity and freight costs and delayed pass-throughs (May-July). Chinese pricing at $1.50-1.70 seen as not a major concern; Shaily priced above $2. Contracts are not cost-plus.

qa_highlights.question: Comfort with 36 million guidance given partner issues in Canada and Brazil?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap in supply must be filled and it still holds most approvals in various markets; it remains confident in guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Time to reach $10 million revenue in Consumer Electronics?
qa_highlights.answer: Management projected 24-30 months, explicitly not guidance.

qa_highlights.question: Status of the Consumer Electronics plant and Semiconductor Trays?
qa_highlights.answer: Commercial supply started; 5 components to be supplied before FY-end. Semiconductor Trays: INR5 crore initial investment; Consumer Electronics plant INR80-100 crore.

qa_highlights.question: Development status of emergency use, reusable and on-body injectors?
qa_highlights.answer: Reusable auto-injector to be tested this month or next and shown at CPHI Milan. Emergency use program ~18 months in, targeted for closure by end-FY27. On-body injector via partnership, developed from the Mira prototype.

risks_watch: Supplier-side execution on the new pen line: speed up only ~9% so far; extra equipment not yet received (expected ~30% uplift, targeted before Q1 FY27 quarter end); second line ships only after supplier reaches 80%+ efficiency and passes FAT.

FY27 36 million pen guidance versus partner supply gaps: management said the gap must be filled and it remains confident, while Ritesh Shah flagged supply issues at a partner in Canada and Brazil (impurities and technical issues, unconfirmed on call).
Gross margin normalisation by Q3 FY27 depends on delayed pass-throughs (May-July) taking effect; watch sequential margin trend and polymer/freight costs.

Chinese GLP-1 pen pricing at $1.50-1.70 vs Shaily above $2; annual price reviews rather than cost-plus means pricing pressure can flow into margins at renewal; management is considering a response to patent-infringing products.
Consumer segment down 24% YoY with management not providing FY27 guidance beyond keeping it near FY26 levels; UK subsidiary revenue dip called timing, with no growth guidance given.

Milestones pending: Semiconductor revenue from Q4 FY27, Consumer Electronics plant start-up update next quarter, Abu Dhabi plant in production by end-FY28, reusable auto-injector testing and CPHI Milan showcase, emergency use program closure by end-FY27.

summary.management_tone: Confident on Healthcare volume growth and the 36 million pen guidance, with repeated 'we should be able to go beyond 36 million' and 'we still remain confident of the guidance'. Cautious and evasive on specifics: declined to give UK subsidiary or customer-level detail, refused a Consumer segment full-year answer, and disclaimed a $10 million revenue timeline as 'not guidance'.
